note: Famous ski circuits. Text written for drop; figures are approximate and taken from the official pages listed under sources. Piste lines come from OpenStreetMap (ODbL).

circuits.title: Der Weisse Ring
circuits.summary: The legendary loop of Lech Zürs am Arlberg: 22 km and about 5,500 m of vertical through Lech, Zürs, Zug and Oberlech, all on skis. It runs on easy and intermediate slopes and is signposted all the way round. A half-day classic.
tips: Follow the Der Weisse Ring signs: the whole loop is signposted.
You can join it in Lech (Rüfikopfbahn), in Zürs (Seekopf or Zürsersee) or in Zug (Zugerbergbahn).
Madloch–Zug (170) is a ski route, not a groomed piste.
In late winter, ski Lech and Oberlech first: they turn to spring snow before Zürs and Zug.

circuits.title: Sellaronda · orange variant
circuits.summary: A signposted alternative for one stretch of the clockwise Sellaronda in Val Gardena. Same orange signs, different pistes: handy when the main line is crowded.
tips: Follow the orange Sellaronda signs; the variant rejoins the main loop.

circuits.title: Sellaronda · clockwise (orange)
circuits.summary: The classic day in the Dolomites: a full loop around the Sella massif through Val Gardena, Alta Badia, Arabba and Val di Fassa, over four passes. Clockwise you follow the orange signs. The pistes are mostly reds and blues, so a confident intermediate can do it; what makes it hard is the length and the lift queues.
tips: Start by 10:00 at the latest.
Plan to be past the last pass by about 15:30: lifts close and a taxi back over the pass is long and expensive.
You need the Dolomiti Superski pass, not a local one.

circuits.title: Sellaronda · anticlockwise (green)
circuits.summary: The same loop around the Sella massif in the other direction, following the green signs. Different pistes and lifts from the orange way, so many people ski both on different days.
tips: Start by 10:00 at the latest.
Plan to be past the last pass by about 15:30.
You need the Dolomiti Superski pass.

circuits.title: First World War Ski Tour · clockwise
circuits.summary: A long loop around the Col di Lana along the old 1915–17 front line, linking Alta Badia, Arabba, Marmolada, Civetta, Cortina and the Lagazuoi. Wartime tunnels and trenches along the way, and a couple of stretches by bus or ski taxi that are part of the route.
tips: A full day: be on the first lift.
Check that the Marmolada and Lagazuoi lifts are running before you set off.
Bring cash or a card for the ski taxi section.

match: first world war ski tour counterclockwise
circuits.title: First World War Ski Tour · anticlockwise
circuits.summary: The Great War loop in the other direction: the same valleys and historic sites around the Col di Lana, with a different order of pistes and lifts.
tips: A full day: be on the first lift.
Check that the Marmolada and Lagazuoi lifts are running.

circuits.title: Super 8
circuits.summary: A figure-of-eight above Passo Falzarego near Cortina, linking the Cinque Torri, Averau, Croda Negra and Lagazuoi. Short, very scenic and not difficult, with a bus or taxi hop in the middle.
tips: About 8 km of the loop is by bus or taxi.
Good half-day if you are staying in Cortina.

circuits.title: Giro delle Cime
circuits.summary: The big loop of the 3 Zinnen Dolomites area: Monte Elmo, Croda Rossa and the pistes towards Comelico, starting from Versciaco or Sesto. A long, varied day with lots of vertical.
tips: One section uses the shuttle bus: check its timetable.
Start from Versciaco or Sesto.

circuits.title: Tauernrunde · red (clockwise)
circuits.summary: Obertauern sits in a bowl on the pass, so its lifts and pistes form a ring around the village. The red round goes clockwise and is the more demanding of the two.
tips: Start and finish in Obertauern village.

circuits.title: Tauernrunde · green (anticlockwise)
circuits.summary: The ring around Obertauern the other way round. The green round is the easier one, a good first lap of the resort.
tips: Start and finish in Obertauern village.

circuits.title: The Challenge
circuits.summary: The biggest circuit of the Skicircus: a loop through Saalbach, Hinterglemm, Leogang and Fieberbrunn. For strong skiers with a full day and good legs.
tips: Start early and keep an eye on the clock: the way back is long.

circuits.title: Hinterglemm round
circuits.summary: One of the signposted circuits of the Skicircus, around the Hinterglemm side of the valley.

circuits.title: Leogang round
circuits.summary: One of the signposted circuits of the Skicircus, linking Leogang with the Saalbach side.

circuits.summary: One of the signposted circuits of the Skicircus, taking in the Tyrolean side towards Fieberbrunn.
